# create-handlr-static

> Scaffold a purely static Handlr site — Vite + Tailwind + custom HTML components
> compiled to static HTML by handlr-build. No PHP backend, no HTMX runtime, no
> client-side state. Just layouts, components, pages, and Tailwind. This file orients
> an AI or a developer building one: how to run it, and how the templating works.

npm package `@phillipsharring/create-handlr-static`. Scaffold a new site:

```bash
npm create @phillipsharring/handlr-static my-site
cd my-site
npm run dev
```

The installer (`bin/create.mjs`) copies the bundled `skeleton/` into your target dir and
runs `npm install`. That's the whole thing — a static site with hot reload in dev and a
compiled `dist/` for production.

## The one engine underneath (read this next)

This skeleton is powered entirely by **handlr-build**. Its `llms.txt` is the
authoritative reference for the templating model, config, and output:

- Build tooling: [../build/llms.txt](../build/llms.txt)
- Prose docs: https://handlr.dev/frontend/build

There is **no** backend or frontend-runtime package here — if you find yourself needing
auth, forms, modals, or API calls, you've outgrown static (see "Graduating" below).

## Commands

```bash
npm run dev       # Vite dev server, pages baked on the fly
npm run build     # vite build && handlr-build-pages → dist/
npm run preview   # preview the built dist/
```

## Directory layout

```
my-site/
├── content/
│   ├── layouts/base.html        # the HTML shell with [[app]], [[title]], [[pageHead]] slots
│   ├── components/callout.html  # reusable custom-tag templates (<callout>, …)
│   └── pages/                   # one HTML file per route (index.html → /, about.html → /about/)
├── public/                      # static assets copied as-is
├── src/
│   ├── app.js                   # Vite entry (imports the CSS)
│   └── styles/style.css         # Tailwind v4
├── site.config.js               # [[placeholders]] (siteName, copyright, …) + optional modules
└── vite.config.js               # tailwind + handlr-build dev plugin
```

## Authoring model (brief — full detail in the build llms.txt)

A **page** is a body plus optional leading directives:

```html
<layout name="base" title="About" />
<page-head><meta name="description" content="About us." /></page-head>

<h1>About</h1>
<callout type="info">We build tools.</callout>
```

- `<layout name="…" />` picks `content/layouts/<name>.html` (default `base`); the body
  fills its `[[app]]` slot, `<page-head>` fills `[[pageHead]]`.
- **Layout placeholders**: `[[app]]`, `[[title]]`, `[[cssHref]]`, `[[jsSrc]]`,
  `[[pageHead]]`, `[[gitSha]]`, and `[[<anyKey>]]` for every `site.config.js` key.
- **Components** (`content/components/<name>.html`): invoke as `<callout>` (single-word
  tag matching a file), `<my-thing>` (hyphenated), or `<component name="…"/>`. Inside:
  `[[prop]]` (escaped), `[[{prop}]]` (raw), `[[slot]]`, `[[#if flag]]…[[else]]…[[/if]]`.
- **Routing** is file-based: `content/pages/about.html` → `/about/`. Bracketed segments
  (`[slug].html`) are dynamic. Files prefixed `_` are skipped.
- `flatRoutes` / `minify` / `devCss` are set once in `site.config.js`.

## Graduating to a full app

Static covers content sites (marketing, docs, landing pages). The moment you need a
backend, auth, forms, modals, or live data, scaffold the full-stack skeleton instead —
same build model, plus the PHP framework and the HTMX runtime:

```bash
composer create-project phillipsharring/handlr-app my-app
```

See [../app/llms.txt](../app/llms.txt).
